title: Chapter 6 Quiz: The Admin Interface
description: Test your knowledge of Django’s admin site, customization, and features.

questions.question: Which file do you edit to register a model with the admin?
questions.explanation: `admin.py` is where you configure the admin interface for your app.

questions.question: The admin interface can be accessed without creating a superuser first.
questions.explanation: False. You need at least one superuser to log into the admin.

questions.question: Which attribute of ModelAdmin controls the columns displayed in the list view?
questions.explanation: `list_display` is the correct attribute.

questions.question: To enable searching on a model’s title field in the admin, you would set `______ = ('title',)`.
questions.explanation: `search_fields` tells Django which fields to include in the search box.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `list_filter`?
options: To filter the list of objects by specific values
To exclude certain fields from the list view
To filter which users can see the admin
To filter the number of records per page
questions.explanation: `list_filter` adds sidebar filters based on field values.

questions.question: You can use a custom method in `list_display` to show computed values.
questions.explanation: Yes, you can define a method on the ModelAdmin class and include its name in `list_display`.

questions.question: Which inline style displays related objects in a table row format?
questions.explanation: `TabularInline` uses a table layout; `StackedInline` uses a block layout.

questions.question: The `extra` attribute on an inline class controls how many ______ forms are shown.
questions.explanation: `extra` defines how many blank forms to display for adding new related objects.

questions.question: What is the default admin action that Django provides?
questions.explanation: By default, the admin includes a "Delete selected" action.

questions.question: You can only create one ModelAdmin per model.
questions.explanation: False. You can have multiple ModelAdmin classes and register the same model under different names using `admin.site.register(Model, AdminClass)`.

questions.question: How do you group fields into collapsible sections in the edit form?
questions.explanation: `fieldsets` allows you to organize fields into groups, optionally with the 'collapse' class.

questions.question: The decorator `@admin.______` can be used to register a model with a custom ModelAdmin class.
questions.explanation: `@admin.register(Post)` is the decorator syntax.

questions.question: Which attribute would you use to prevent a field from being edited in the admin?
questions.explanation: `readonly_fields` makes fields display but not editable.

questions.question: Admin actions must return an HttpResponse if they perform an action that changes the page.
questions.explanation: If an action performs a redirect or returns a file (like CSV), it must return an HttpResponse. Otherwise, it can just modify the queryset and return None.

questions.question: Which method would you use to add a custom action to the admin?
options: define a function and add to actions
questions.explanation: You define a function and add its name to the `actions` list in ModelAdmin.

questions.question: To make a method appear as a boolean icon in list_display, you can set the attribute `______ = True` on the method.
questions.explanation: Assigning `method.boolean = True` makes Django render it as a checkmark/cross icon.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `prepopulated_fields` in ModelAdmin?
options: To fill a field based on another field’s value (e.g., slug from title)
To populate fields with default values
To pre‑fill forms with test data
questions.explanation: `prepopulated_fields` automatically populates a field (like a slug) from another field as you type.

questions.question: The admin interface can be completely overridden with custom templates.
questions.explanation: True. You can override admin templates by placing templates with the same names in your project's template directory.

questions.question: Which setting controls the URL where the admin is accessible?
options: It's defined in the project's urls.py
questions.explanation: The admin URL is set in the project's `urls.py` with `path('admin/', admin.site.urls)`.

questions.question: To limit the number of items displayed per page in the changelist, use the `______` attribute.
questions.explanation: `list_per_page = 25` will paginate after 25 items.
